title: Enlargement extends heading memory as fluctuating input changes domain dynamics
role: Size-dependent heading persistence, edge drift and secondary-domain competition under fluctuating input.
legend: A. Drifting peaks, same-rate null relocations and perimeter-rate null relocations give size exponents 2, 0 and −1. Null kymograph widths follow circumference; time increases upward. Autocorrelations C(ℓ) use solid C20 and dotted C60 curves. The null relocations are illustrative whole-peak moves, distinct from measured dominant-region replacements and birth-to-takeover events.

B. Larger rings retain heading across stronger fluctuating input. Input fraction f sets the ensemble mean to f times the native reference (Wave-pinning 0.1; Holmes 1; Spring 4; Goryachev 6.4). Input is positive lognormal, mean × exp(σZ−σ²/2), with unit-variance Gaussian driving field Z and σ=1. The spatial parameter ℓ and OU correlation time τ are 1.5 and 50 in chemical models; Spring uses basal-physical ℓ=0.15 and τ=5, with physical ℓ scaling with its changing circumference. Local size exponents α and noise-tolerance folds use model hues and light-to-dark circumference ramps. Open symbols in the exponent and drift panels identify conditions flagged as forced by the frozen matched-mean/lower-noise controls; open diamonds in the fold panel identify Goryachev irrespective of forcing; vertical intervals are pointwise 95% whole-history bootstrap intervals. Boundary triangles retain off-scale values. 125/260 local neighborhoods resolve, including 11 Goryachev neighborhoods. Largest-size tolerance folds are Wave-pinning 2.373, Holmes 2.155, Spring 3.088 and Goryachev 4.122. f₁/₂ is the first input crossing of C(ℓ)=0.5 at reference lag 2000 (Spring 200); Spring circumference is multiplied by 20 only in the fold panel.

C. Matched small- and large-ring kymographs are centred on their initial activity heading to the nearest spatial bin. Time increases upward; black outside ticks mark persistent dominant-region replacements. Activity scales are shared within Wave-pinning, Holmes and Spring; Goryachev uses 0–9.2 at C20 and 0–83 at C60. Ensemble C(ℓ) curves are below. A low-contrast initial heading may have weak biological meaning despite a defined numerical centre.

D. Physical within-tenure drift Dₛ is normalized by the smallest size at the same input. Unity gives the equal-physical-drift geometric expectation α=2. Weak-input log–log fits for f≤0.01 give exponents Wave-pinning 1.96–1.99; Holmes 1.94–1.95; Spring 1.87–1.93. The second row shows the existing event-based predicted/observed decay only where f≤0.01 and multiple regions occupy at most 5% of frames. 45/47 eligible point comparisons lie within 15% (Wave-pinning 16/16; Holmes 15/16; Spring 14/14; Goryachev 0/1). These point predictions assign the scored-event mean angular loss to unscored replacements; this remains an assumption. Goryachev uses separate logarithmic ordinate ranges: 10⁻⁷–2 for normalized drift and 0.003–3.3 for decay ratio; other models use 0.2–8 and 0.3–3.3. The actual mean circumference, C̄, enters physical-to-angular conversion. Figure 3D independently predicts this measured drift from deterministic edge responses.

E. i, Certified no-parent secondary births per actual perimeter-time: new tracks persist at least five frames, have a preceding incumbent, and have conservative support enclosures disjoint from all previous regions. Rates are lower bounds; discarded masks prevent exact birth/split classification. ii, Observed incidence of five-frame global dominance by 20τ (1000 chemical units; 100 Spring), conditional on certified births with that follow-up. Inputs f>0.01 are pooled. Distance d subtracts estimated incumbent half-width (preceding full-basin amount divided by twice global contrast h) from the shortest centroid arc. Vertical intervals are 95% whole-history bootstrap intervals. A lower finite-horizon incidence can reflect delayed or less frequent takeover; lifetime success remains unidentified. Figure 2B–C motivates separating initiation from incumbent removal. iii, Native-amplitude-aware signed heading-loss allocation over the condition’s analysis lag. M, shared-region motion; A, coexisting amount; B, track membership including unresolved splits/mergers; R, amplitude/shape/background remainder. Point-region Shapley changes are scaled by mean native endpoint moment amplitude, so pure rigid translation gives M=1, R=0. Components sum exactly to observed heading loss but are descriptive, convention-dependent shares. The symmetric-log color scale is linear within ±0.05 and spans ±1; dots indicate values outside ±1, gray unavailable pairs. The unit-normalized point-region diagnostic and its normalization artefact are preserved in the supplement; eligibility and equations are detailed in Methods.

narrative: Enlargement extends heading memory and raises noise tolerance, while the size advantage weakens as input strengthens. The weak-input drift in Wave-pinning, Holmes and Spring is close to quadratic in input, connecting Figure 4 to the deterministic edge-response test in Figure 3.

Direct event accounting distinguishes persistent secondary onsets from certifiable no-parent births. Certified takeover probability declines with size in each model at a common finite follow-up, but different certification fractions and pooled inputs limit population inference. Per-perimeter birth direction varies by model; it is not a universal consequence of enlargement.

At native moment amplitude, eligible weak-input heading loss is allocated almost entirely to domain motion. As secondary domains appear, membership changes and the amplitude/shape/background remainder can grow; the pattern varies with model and size. This exact accounting remains descriptive, and the original unit-normalized point-region artefact is retained as a supplementary diagnostic.

equations.description: Q is the normalized point-region moment; P=M₁/M₀ is measured from the native field. Its amplitude r prevents the unit-modulus single-region normalization artefact.

equations.math: \Delta P_j=\bar r\,\Delta Q_j\ (j=\mathrm{M,A,B}),\qquad\Delta P_{\mathrm{R}}=\Delta P-\bar r\,\Delta Q
equations.description: The three ΔQ components use the symmetric Shapley convention for motion, coexisting amount and membership; r̄ is mean endpoint native amplitude. R closes the native moment change and includes amplitude variation, shape and background. This is an accounting convention, not causal attribution.
Pooled signed fractions are sums of L_j divided by total measured heading loss. They retain cancellation, can exceed one, and depend on the stated accounting convention; they are not causal shares.
C(ℓ) is activity-heading autocorrelation; C̄ is actual mean circumference. Endpoint eligibility uses |P|≥0.1. Drift closure is shown only at f≤0.01 and multiple-region fraction≤0.05.

measurements: Measure lateral-edge fluctuations, secondary-protrusion births per actual perimeter-time, finite-horizon takeover probability and leading-edge displacement after boundary-straddling photoactivation. Preserve separate WGD-associated cell-size, observed migration and simulated polarity-heading readouts.
limitations: Exact no-overlap birth counts and split counts cannot be recovered for the full campaign because compact records discard native masks/parent IDs. Lower/upper birth bounds and conditional takeovers are reported instead. The global-contrast plateau estimate is not a recovered per-region plateau.

Native clocks are not calibrated between models. A takeover is five-frame global dominance within 20 noise correlation times, not a lifetime success probability. Full-history right censoring, short-followup exclusions and per-condition counts are retained in CSV. Inputs f>0.01 are pooled without reweighting; size cohorts can differ in their event-weighted input composition. A lower incidence by 20τ does not distinguish slower takeover from a lower lifetime probability. A fixed-cohort supplementary incidence curve extends observation to 80τ without extrapolating beyond it.

Heading attribution uses only eligible lag endpoint pairs with measured |P|≥0.1, finite tracked amounts/centroids and all nonzero hybrid totals. Goryachev at f=0.03 has pair coverage 0.666 at C20 but only 0.0109 at C60. Endpoint membership does not reveal events occurring and reversing inside the lag. This algebraic allocation depends on the chosen convention and includes normalized point-region approximation error in its residual.

Historical multiple-front-majority closure point predictions are conditional on scored angles representing unscored replacements: none of 33 point estimates is within 15%, but missing-angle bounds permit agreement within 15% in 24/33 and span unity in 18/33. This cannot generally distinguish omitted heading processes from unscored large-angle replacements. Goryachev’s 37 historical finite point ratios span 0.00575–0.344, with limited dominant-region exposure and angle scoring; missing-angle bounds span unity in 11/37. These diagnostics remain in the supplement and do not motivate the independent exact endpoint allocation.
